All five `utcnow()` calls in `app/` (audit, billing, cache, reports, sessions) now use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`. I added `timezone` to each import. A search finds no `utcnow` left in `app/` or `tests/`.

pytest isn't installed here, so I ran the five test functions directly with `python3 -W error::DeprecationWarning`. All passed with no deprecation warnings.

`reports.header()` output changes. The timestamp now ends in `+00:00`, for example `T generated 2026-10-17T20:13:19+00:00`, where before it had no offset. The test only checks the `"T generated "` prefix, so it still passes. If anything downstream parses that string, it needs to handle the offset.

All stored and returned datetimes are now timezone-aware. Comparing them with naive datetimes from elsewhere will raise `TypeError`. Within this codebase the comparisons in `cache.py` are aware-to-aware, so they work.
